title: Parameter binding sources ([FromBody], [FromRoute], [AsParameters])
hook: Binding source attributes tell ASP.NET Core exactly where each parameter comes from — route segment, query string, header, form, or JSON body. [AsParameters] (.NET 7+) bundles many query fields into one record, which is the cleanest pattern for search and filter endpoints.

blocks.text: Each action or minimal API parameter is bound from a BindingSource: Path (route), Query, Header, Form, Body, or Services (dependency injection). Attributes like [FromRoute], [FromQuery], [FromHeader], [FromBody], and [FromForm] override [ApiController] inference. [AsParameters] marks a type whose public properties are bound individually from route and query — perfect for pagination and search DTOs without ten separate parameters. [FromServices] is explicit DI; most services are injected without an attribute when the type is registered in the container.

entries.plainDefinition: Bind parameter from the HTTP request body (typically JSON). Only one per action.
Bind from URI path segments matched by the route template.
.NET 7+ attribute: bind a record/class properties from route and query in one parameter.
entries.example: GetOrders([AsParameters] OrderQuery query) where OrderQuery has Page, PageSize, Status.

entries.plainDefinition: Resolved from DI container, not from the HTTP request.
entries.example: IOrderService orders — no attribute needed when type is registered.

blocks.text: Explicit binding sources prevent ambiguous matches — especially when a simple type could come from route or query. [AsParameters] keeps signatures readable and makes OpenAPI reflect a structured query object. Wrong sources cause null parameters, 415 Unsupported Media Type, or silent wrong values. Senior interviews test [AsParameters], header-based versioning, and the single-body rule.

blocks.title: [AsParameters] rules
blocks.body: Properties must be bindable from route or query (simple types, enums, nullable). No [FromBody] properties inside an [AsParameters] type. Works in controllers and minimal APIs. Prefer a record for immutability.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: Check explicit attribute
items.body: [FromQuery] on parameter or property wins over inference.

items.title: Apply [ApiController] inference
items.body: If no attribute: complex type → body on POST/PUT; simple type → route then query.

items.title: [AsParameters] expansion
items.body: Binder treats each property as a separate parameter with route/query sources.

items.title: DI resolution
items.body: Types in DI are satisfied from Services binding source, not HTTP.

items.title: Bind and validate
items.body: Each source reads from ValueProvider (route values, query collection, header dictionary).

diagram.title: [AsParameters] binding flow
diagram.source:
flowchart LR
  URL["/api/orders?page=2&status=Shipped"] --> AP[AsParameters OrderQuery]
  AP --> P1[Page = 2\nfrom Query]
  AP --> P2[Status = Shipped\nfrom Query]
  AP --> P3[Sort default\noptional query]

snippet.label: Explicit binding sources on a controller action
snippet.explanation: [FromRoute] and [FromQuery] disambiguate simple types. [FromHeader] reads custom headers — useful for correlation IDs and feature flags. [FromServices] is optional but documents DI explicitly.

snippet.label: [AsParameters] record for search and pagination
snippet.explanation: [AsParameters] collapses four query fields into one type. OpenAPI generators emit a single query object schema. Defaults in the record apply when query keys are absent.

snippet.label: [AsParameters] mixing route and query properties
snippet.explanation: Properties can specify [FromRoute] or [FromQuery] inside an [AsParameters] type. This pattern replaces long parameter lists on multi-tenant list endpoints.

snippet.label: Single body rule and form file binding
snippet.explanation: Only one [FromBody] per request. File uploads use [FromForm] and multipart/form-data. [Consumes] restricts content types and improves OpenAPI accuracy.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Putting [FromBody] on a property inside [AsParameters] — not supported. Using [FromQuery] on a complex type without a custom binder — only top-level properties bind. Forgetting [FromRoute] when route and query names collide. Relying on inference for PUT with both id in route and body — specify [FromRoute] on id.

blocks.text: BindingSource.Metadata is attached to parameters for OpenAPI and client generators. [AsParameters] uses AsParametersBindingConvention — internally expands to property binders. For header-based API versioning, [FromHeader(Name = "X-Api-Version")] on an [AsParameters] property keeps version next to other query params in one DTO. Custom BindingSource can be created for advanced scenarios (custom ValueProvider). In minimal APIs, parameter order does not affect binding — only types and attributes matter. Production tip: log binding failures with action name and ModelState keys; spike in 400s often means client query contract drift.

blocks.title: [AsParameters] vs alternatives
rows: Properties must be simple — no nested body

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Not knowing [AsParameters] exists in .NET 7+ for query bundling. Claiming multiple [FromBody] parameters work. Unable to explain difference between [FromServices] and constructor injection — same container, different binding stage. Saying headers are bound by default without [FromHeader].

interviewTakeaways: [FromRoute], [FromQuery], [FromHeader], [FromBody], [FromForm] explicitly set where each value is read from the request.
Only one [FromBody] per request — use [AsParameters] or [FromQuery] for composite list/filter inputs on GET.
[AsParameters] (.NET 7+) binds record properties from route and query — preferred for pagination and search DTOs.

60s: Binding sources disambiguate route vs query vs body. ApiController infers defaults. AsParameters bundles query fields into one type for clean signatures and OpenAPI. Services come from DI, not HTTP.
Follow-up: how would you bind a nested filter object from query string?
commonPitfalls: Saying 'you can bind two JSON bodies' gets you rejected — HTTP has one body stream.
Using [FromBody] on GET list endpoints — use [AsParameters] with query instead.
Strong answer: 'Explicit attributes override inference. AsParameters for search DTOs. One body rule. FromHeader for correlation and versioning. DI types skip HTTP binding.'
introducedIn: Binding attributes from ASP.NET Core 1.0; [AsParameters] in .NET 7

jsTsCorrelations.note: const { page, status } = req.query is manual [AsParameters]. ASP.NET binds and type-converts in one step — '2' becomes int 2 with error on invalid.
class PaginationDto { @Type(() => Number) page: number } mirrors [AsParameters] with implicit conversion. Nest needs class-transformer; ASP.NET uses TypeConverter infrastructure.
